proxy_language: Cusco Quechua (Southern Quechua), the Inka court language; Classical Colonial Quechua as recorded by Domingo de Santo Tomás (1560) and Gonçález Holguín (1608)
proxy_rationale: 'Mountain-and-Mother Court' reads as a later Andean state court centered on apu/mountain veneration and Pachamama/Mama (earth-mother, Coya/Mamacuna) cults, i.e. the Inka court. Cusco Quechua is attested and well documented, so it is the best proxy; the link is medium because the culture's real identity is only a label and Aymara or Puquina court languages are also possible.
phonology: Three vowels /a i u/ (written a, i, u; e and o are allophones near uvular q, not written in standard orthography). Stops and affricates in three-way series: plain (p t ch k q), aspirated (ph th chh kh qh), ejective (p' t' ch' k' q'); Cusco has all three. Fricatives s, h; nasals m n ñ; laterals l ll; rhotic r; glides w y. Uvular q contrasts with velar k. Stress penultimate.
phonotactics: Syllable shapes (C)V(C). No initial vowel clusters and no vowel sequences within a root (hiatus is rare, with y/w between). Native roots begin with a single consonant or a vowel; no initial consonant clusters. Medial clusters are limited to coda C plus onset C (e.g. -nk-, -mp-, -rq-, -sp-, -yk-). Roots are usually 2 to 3 syllables. Spanish loans add e and o, which should be avoided in pre-contact-feel names. Words end in a vowel or in a limited set of consonants (-n, -s, -y, -q, -k, -m, -l, -r), mostly via suffixes.
orthography: Modern Quechua practical orthography (Academia Mayor de la Lengua Quechua, Cusco): a i u; p t k q ch; ph th kh qh chh; p' t' k' q' ch'; s h; m n ñ; l ll r; w y. Apostrophe marks ejectives, h marks aspiration. Avoid c, z, v, b, d, f, g, j, x, e and o.
morphology: Agglutinative, exclusively suffixing, SOV. Roots are nouns or verbs. Nominal suffixes: plural -kuna, genitive -pa (-qpa after vowel), possessive -n (3rd), -y (1st), -yki (2nd), accusative -ta, locative -pi, dative -man, ablative -manta, instrumental -wan, 'and/with' -wan, limitative -kama, reflexive-intensive -lla (only/just), topic -qa. Verb nominalizers: -q agentive ('one who does'), -na instrumental/place ('thing for doing'), -y infinitive/action noun, -sqa past participle ('done'), -yniyuq/-yuq 'possessor of X'. Derivational: -wasi 'house of', -pata 'bank/terrace'. Reduplication is used for intensity and repetition, e.g. raphi raphi.
compounding: Head-final: modifier precedes head (juk'a wasi 'small house'). Noun-noun compounds and genitive phrases put the possessor first: 'X of Y' = Y-pa X-n, e.g. Inti-pa wasi-n 'house of the sun'. Common bare compounds use juxtaposition without a linker: Inti Raymi 'sun festival', Mama Quilla 'mother moon'. Agent names: object + verb-q, e.g. wasi-ruraq 'house-maker', yachay-wasi 'knowledge-house' (school). Place names often add -pata, -marka, -pampa, -qocha.
noun_phrase_order: Modifier before head: adjective/numeral/possessor + noun (hatun mama 'great mother', kimsa apu 'three mountains'); relative clauses with -q or -sqa also precede the head; plural -kuna and case suffixes attach to the end of the whole noun phrase.
sources: Domingo de Santo Tomás, Grammatica o arte de la lengua general de los indios de los reynos del Peru, 1560
Diego Gonçález Holguín, Vocabulario de la lengua general de todo el Perú llamada lengua qquichua o del Inca, 1608
Willem Adelaar with Pieter Muysken, The Languages of the Andes, 2004
Academia Mayor de la Lengua Quechua, Diccionario Quechua-Español-Quechua, 1995
notes: Existing game strings (Sucilu, Hina pa misnas, Yiwir) mix Quechua-like -pa/-nas with non-Quechua shapes; -nas is not a Quechua plural (use -kuna). No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word since the language is not Goidelic. Names should avoid Spanish-influenced e/o and avoid claiming specific Inka royal titles that are historically bound to real figures.
